generic: If you hear the foghorn this far up, it’s time to bring the boats in.
The lab light was on when I went to bed. It was still on when I took the bread over.
I leave the gate unlatched for my Growlithe. He won’t go near the long grass after dark.
rivalAhead: Your rival asked if you’d picked yet. Twice, actually.
They’re waiting by the gate. I offered them a chair. Don’t think they heard me.

generic: I scrub these steps every morning. By lunch you can write your name in the quarry dust.
See the little house by the cut? The foreman still leaves a lamp in the window on payday.
The shift bell just went. If you want a quiet look at the Gym, go before they wash up.
preGym: I take sandwiches to the Gym on match days. Three rounds can feel like a whole shift.
My cousin went in with one partner and came out looking for another. Check your party before you go.
postGym: The night shift heard you won. They asked me to leave your name on the board.
First badge? Go on, let me see it. My old one’s worn smooth.

generic: The Tutor drinks their tea cold. By the time they remember it, they’ve taught half the room.
The stall with the red cloth sells stones. Ask the seller which one your partner needs.
Someone left an empty Egg basket by the inn stove. The matron won’t let me move it.
preGym: The Gym’s through the café courtyard. If you smell coffee, you’ve gone far enough.
There’s a place to sit by the stone stall if your partner needs a minute before the match.
postGym: They asked me to put the kettle on when you got back. You could hear the match from here.
The Tutor was at the back of the Gym. Saw what you did with that last turn.

generic: They’ve got three maps in the academy and every one calls the old road something different.
Best time for a practice match is after the last lecture. You’ll have to move the desks yourself.
There’s still a survey notebook in the lost-property drawer. Nobody remembers who handed it in.
preGym: The practice board’s open to challengers. The students are fairly good at spotting a weak switch.
Take the side door if the lecture’s still going. The Gym is across the yard.
postGym: They made your last match homework. The kids are still arguing about the switch.
You can have your seat back by the stove. We’ve been saving it since the bell.
rivalAhead: Your rival borrowed a practice room. Left three chalk circles on the floor and didn’t say goodbye.
They asked which way you’d be taking. I said I’d been inside all morning.

generic: Take the stairs if you only need one thing. The store puts all the little purchases by the lifts.
The clerk can tell you which floor has what. I’d ask before following the painted arrows.
Don’t park your bike by the loading doors. They lock that alley when the last wagon leaves.
preGym: Last time I went to a match upstairs, I missed the first round looking for the right door.
The store’s open after the match as well. You can pick up supplies when the crowd thins.
postGym: We watched you get the badge on the display TVs. The fridges kept beeping through the good bit.
Someone put the match score in the window on floor four. I waited till the ink dried to look.

generic: You can follow the boardwalk from the ranger huts to the casino without crossing a road.
If the ranger tells you to put the bait down, put it down. The Krabby can hear the bucket.
My brother takes a set purse into the casino. Last week he took the train home.
preGym: The wind’s mean after sundown. I’d get the Gym done before it turns.
Most of the crowd comes up from the boardwalk. They’ll point you to the entrance.
postGym: The ranger at the far gate asked whether the noise was for you. I said it probably was.
They’re still moving your match crowd out of the casino doorway. Take the lake path if you’re leaving.

generic: If you’re meeting someone after the late shift, pick a bay number. There are too many gates marked Exit.
The square screen’s stuck on the old Champion’s entrance again. Give it a minute.
Somebody’s been hanging dry blankets on the freight fence. They’re gone by first bell.
preGym: The arena doors open early. The warm-up room’s quieter if you want to look at your team.
My shift pays for the cheap seats. I hope you give them something to talk about tomorrow.
postGym: I saw your badge come up on the square screen. Had to cross twice before the light changed.
Half the arena had you down to lose. Give them till morning to admit it.
rivalAhead: Your rival asked when the last gate closes. I said it doesn’t.
There’s a note for you at the Gym desk. The clerk knows whose it is.

generic: Take the lower path if there’s ice on the rail. A lamp can look awfully close up here.
Colress moved his bench away from the draft. If you hear tools, you’ve got the right door.
The relay hut lights up after midnight sometimes. We stopped checking the roster.
preGym: The Gym steps are dry today. That’s about the only favor the mountain gives you.
If you want to change your build first, go while Buck’s still at his bench.
postGym: The veterans finally made room on the bench. They’d like to hear how the last fight went.
That’s the cathedral bell you can hear. Wait for a gap in the wind.

generic: They ring the big bell once for each challenger. You can hear the smaller one from the road.
If you’re heading out tonight, ask the keeper when the gate closes. He’s usually on the stair.
The cloth on the altar’s been mended four times. See if you can find the first seam.
preGym: I’ll leave the kettle on. There are still two lamps lit inside the Gym.
The Gym keeper can hear the doors from the top stair. You won’t need to knock twice.
postGym: Eight? All right. Put the case back inside your coat. The walk to the Plateau is cold.
Somebody in a mask asked about you this morning. Left before I could point out the Gym.

generic: Registration’s through the second door. The first one leads to the broadcast booth.
My brother took ages to come out of that hall. I walked around the building until my feet went numb.
See the empty frame at the end? The clerk polishes it along with all the others.
The Hall got your name right. I checked. There’s still someone waiting down the corridor.
Did the lights flicker when you came through? The electrician packed up hours ago.
I’ve got your coat here. If you’re going down that corridor, leave it with me a little longer.
You can get a seat in the Crucible just about any night. Bring a coat if you sit by the service door.
I recognize the name on your badge case. Down here, somebody will still ask you to prove it.
They used to prop the service door with a brick. Ask the night clerk what happened to it.
